content.text:
<document id=DOC_req_years_eight>
Required: 8 years of backend engineering experience.
</document>

<document id=DOC_summary_no_dates>
Backend engineering across transactional services, most recently a
settlement pipeline handling 40,000 orders a day. Previously worked on
payment reconciliation and inventory systems.
</document>

Rewrite the candidate summary above to match the posting requirement.

If years of experience are neither stated nor calculable, ask me for the
figure and tell me what it costs not to supply it.

response.text:
The summary doesn't state your years of experience, and there are no dates or role durations to calculate them from.

**How many years of backend engineering experience do you have?** If it's not a round number, give me the start date of your first backend role.

**What it costs to leave it out:**

- **You may be screened out automatically.** "8 years" reads as a hard requirement. Applicant tracking systems and recruiters often filter on an explicit figure, so a summary without one can be rejected before anyone sees your settlement pipeline work.
- **Your scope argument loses its anchor.** Handling 40,000 orders a day suggests seniority, but a reviewer can't tell whether that took 3 years or 12 to reach.
- **I can't fill the gap.** I won't invent or imply a number, so without the figure the rewrite can only point at experience, not show that you meet the requirement.

**Draft with a placeholder**, ready once you give me the number:

> Backend engineer with **[X] years** of experience building transactional services. Most recently built and operated a settlement pipeline processing 40,000 orders per day. Prior work includes payment reconciliation and inventory systems.

If X is 8 or more, this meets the requirement directly. If it's under 8, tell me and I'll reshape the summary to lead with scope and impact instead.
